subject: Hybrid rebate ladder + true-up proration — legal pricing redlines
messages:
From: Trevor Cole <trevor.cole@novumhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>; procurement@novumhealth.com
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novumhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on your pricing ladder and month-proration for true-ups

Naomi — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement had a few follow-ups after reviewing the draft pricing schedule: we want clarity on how the rebate ladder phases interact with mid-quarter true-ups, and how you plan to prorate partial-month usage when an account migrates between bundles.

Specific asks:
- If the customer crosses a higher band mid-billing-cycle, do you apply the higher band pro rata for the remainder of the cycle or only at the next invoice?
- Your current draft has a variable rebate that resets annually. Can we get language to allow a carry-forward of unused rebate up to one quarter?
- The order form includes a floor and a cap but no explicit invoice rounding rule — procurement prefers amounts rounded to the nearest dollar and a small-statement of the rounding rule.

I've attached the annotated procurement checklist. Can you and legal confirm whether Redwood will accept a 90-day carry-forward cap (max $50k) and pro rata mid-cycle uplift?

Trevor
Senior Director, Procurement
Novum Health

Attachment: procurement_checklist_9081.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Trevor Cole <trevor.cole@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novumhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on your pricing ladder and month-proration for true-ups

Trevor — appreciate the clear list. High level answers below; I’ll loop in legal for precise redline language.

1) Mid-cycle band movement: Our standard is to bill on actuals for the invoice period and reconcile at true-up. Practically that means usage in the billing period will be billed at the band(s) actually consumed; if a customer moves up a band mid-cycle, incremental usage is charged at the higher band for the remainder of that period and we show an adjusted true-up on the next invoice. We can formalize this in the order form with a pro rata uplift clause.

2) Carry-forward: We can offer a carry-forward for unused rebate credits up to one quarter (90 days) with a cap — your proposed $50k cap is within reason, but want legal to approve the exact cap and fallbacks.

3) Rounding: Happy to add an invoice rounding rule: amounts rounded to the nearest dollar; credit carry-forward tracked to cents but rounded on the statement.

I'll attach a draft MA-plan with our proposed wording and a redline we can circulate to legal. If that looks OK to you, we can move to a marked-up order form and DocuSign.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Enterprise Growth — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MA-plan.xlsx (proposal), summary-notes.txt (notes stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Novum — pricing asks (need legal redline + pricing guidance)

Laura / Karthik — forwarding Novum’s procurement questions and my suggested commercial responses. Can you weigh in on the order-form language below and confirm whether Legal is comfortable with: (a) pro rata mid-cycle uplift (we bill incremental usage at the higher band for remainder of period; reconcile at next invoice), (b) one-quarter (90 day) carry-forward of rebates subject to a $50k cap, and (c) an invoice rounding clause that states amounts are rounded to the nearest dollar for customer-facing statements.

Key constraints to consider for Legal: we want to avoid open-ended credits that could sit on the ledger beyond a reasonable window; any carry-forward should expire after 90 days and default to offset future invoices (no cash refunds). Also watch for language that inadvertently creates a guaranteed minimum or implies a billing forgiveness.

Suggested redline language (for inclusion in Exhibit B — Pricing Schedule):
- "Mid-Billing Period Band Adjustment": "If Customer’s monthly usage moves to a higher pricing band during an invoice period, Redwood will charge the incremental usage at the higher band for the remainder of that invoice period; an accounting true-up reflecting band movement will appear on the next invoice."
- "Rebate Carry-Forward": "Unused rebates accrued during any quarter may be carried forward for up to 90 days following the end of that quarter, not to exceed Fifty Thousand Dollars (USD $50,000). Carry-forward credits will be applied against subsequent invoices and are non-refundable."
- "Invoice Rounding": "All invoice line amounts will be rounded to the nearest whole U.S. Dollar for customer-facing invoices; internal accounting may track cents for reconciliation."

Please review and either mark changes in Novum_Pricing_Redline_v2.pdf or tell me if we should push back on carry-forward duration / cap. Hoping to have a legal-marked copy by Monday so we can move to signature.

Thanks — Naomi

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Trevor Cole <trevor.cole@novumhealth.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novumhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Aug 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novum — pricing asks (need legal redline + pricing guidance)

Naomi — reviewed. High-level: we can accept the commercial approach with three edits to protect Redwood:
1) Limit on carry-forward application: credits may only be used against the same SKU family and may not be transferred across subsidiaries.
2) Expiry / remediation: credits expire after 90 days and any unused balance thereafter is forfeited; in the event of customer insolvency, credits are subordinate to other creditor claims.
3) Clarify that mid-cycle band adjustment is bounded: if the customer’s usage both increases and decreases in the same invoice period, netting rules apply and we will calculate billable amounts based on daily usage slices to avoid double-crediting.

I have updated the draft redline (Novum_Pricing_Redline_v2.pdf) with the exact clause wording and a single-line option for invoice rounding (nearest dollar, with cents tracked internally). I recommend we keep the $50k cap but replace any absolute dollar number with "not to exceed the lesser of $50,000 or 10% of the quarter’s committed spend" if you want additional protection — let me know which you prefer.

If Trevor accepts these edits, I’ll generate a clean order form and upload to DocuSign.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Novum_Pricing_Redline_v2.pdf (redline stub)
